extraction.Name: Aloyseus Monroe
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee to his 143 acre allotment when it was issued, September 29, 1919, but that he was told that it would be taxed just the same as if he had accepted the patent in fee, so he took the patent in fee to this allotment
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold the place to Jack Stotts
extraction.Buyer: Jack Stotts, paying down $50.00 on the deal, and promising to pay the $650.00 due on the agreement in about ten days, which was done
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: the taxes got behind for three years, and, in 1922, he sold the place; deponent paid the back taxes out of this $650.00; and that this was his only reason in selling the place
extraction.Occupation/Income: works in the coal mines, on ranches and farms some for himself; and that these three things are the only sources of his income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; his health is rather poor, having had a broken leg, and he now has rheumatism in it; that he is single; that he helps to support his mother; that he has no one else to support; did not sell his land for any debts incurred prior to the receipt of his patent in fee; has never received any help from the County, State Government nor the United States Government; considers that he got a poor price for his place; County of Shannon; sworn February 2, 1929 | TASK 3 BULK TRIBE INFERENCE 2026-04-29: Tribe field set to 'Pine Ridge' based on directory provenance (record is filed in pine_ridge_*/extractions/, which corresponds to the NARA RG 75 Pine Ridge Vol 1, Vol 2, and Vol 3 bound volumes of Circular 2464 responses). 67 such records were originally 'not stated'; 6 received BLM-confirmed substantive patches in the same transaction; the remaining 61 (this record's batch) are inferred from directory and geographic/naming evidence. Inference is rebuttable — any record can be re-evaluated via BLM cross-reference if its Pine Ridge affiliation is questioned.
